- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–7 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: add 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; adjust downward by 1–2% for days 1–7 if sentiment is mixed or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by negative sentiment, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by positive sentiment, model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.
